- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model under-forecasts; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently under-forecasts in early 30-day window (first 5–7 days); apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Forecast should not exceed 2.5% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.30) and recent price is rising >1.5%.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid “sentiment trap.”
